items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The change is short and well commented. The comment explains why the base alias is missing ('e.g. Model.objects.all()'), and the code style matches the surrounding compiler code.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: It reuses the existing query.get_initial_alias() helper inside single_alias and leaves Collector, QuerySet.delete and the backends untouched. The `if all(... == 0 ...)` guard adds a little complexity but avoids an extra ref_alias increment. No dead code.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: No new error paths or magic constants. The guard calls get_initial_alias() only when no alias is referenced, so refcounts stay unchanged for joined or filtered queries. The delete, delete_regress and model_inheritance test suites pass.

items.name: Subquery dropped only for genuine single-table deletes
items.name_zh: 仅在真正单表删除时去掉子查询
items.evidence: The root cause is fixed in single_alias by registering the base alias before counting. The agent's own checks show filter(avatar__desc=...) still produces a JOIN or pk IN subquery, while .all() produces 'DELETE FROM "delete_user"'. There is no backend-specific branch. The hidden tests passed: F2P 1/1, P2P 52/52.
